page: Oracle Cloud Infrastructure BM.Standard2.52 is a bare metal instance belonging to the Standard server family. Built on the x86_64 architecture, it is powered by Intel Xeon 8167M processors operating at a nominal clock frequency of 2.0 GHz. The system provides 52 physical cores and 104 dedicated vCPUs with two execution threads per core. Because it is deployed as bare metal hardware, all CPU resources are dedicated directly to the operating environment without hypervisor overhead or resource contention from neighboring tenants.

The server is equipped with 768.0 GB of system memory, translating to 7.38 GB of RAM per vCPU. The BM.Standard2.52 configuration includes no onboard local storage, requiring persistent operating system files and data volumes to be mounted via remote cloud block storage solutions. Accelerated graphical hardware is not included, as the instance features zero GPUs. Network provisioning includes one complimentary public IPv4 address.

In terms of qualitative efficiency, BM.Standard2.52 maximizes core density and memory footprint within a single physical host, offering consistent execution paths for thread-heavy computations. The lack of onboard storage shifts disk throughput dependencies to remote block volumes, which represents a structural tradeoff for disk-intensive services. With its substantial memory pool and 104 parallel execution threads, the instance aligns with enterprise resource planning systems, high-density container clustering, continuous integration build clusters, and distributed batch processing workloads.
description: Oracle Cloud Infrastructure BM.Standard2.52 is a dedicated bare metal server engineered for high-concurrency enterprise workloads. The hardware platform is powered by Intel Xeon 8167M processors operating at a base clock frequency of 2.0 GHz on the x86_64 architecture. This configuration provides 52 physical CPU cores and 104 virtual CPUs via simultaneous multithreading, accompanied by 768.0 GB of system memory, providing approximately 7.38 GB of memory per core. The server contains no integrated local storage and operates without dedicated GPU hardware accelerators, relying on external network-attached cloud storage for persistent disk needs. A single complimentary public IPv4 address is provisioned by default. The dedicated physical core allocation removes hypervisor contention, delivering consistent execution for large-scale enterprise deployments. These architectural characteristics position BM.Standard2.52 for multi-threaded applications, memory-intensive backend services, container host infrastructure, ERP systems, and batch data processing pipelines.
